subject: Dedicated GPU SKU strategy: memory-window vs batch-throughput for LuminaHealth pilot
messages:

Cc: procurement@luminahealth.com

Subject: Pilot sizing: memory-heavy triage flows + high QPS summary

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the call this morning — quick summary and a request. Our pilot will drive two distinct workloads: (1) a triage assistant that needs 14k token context windows for patient records and is latency-sensitive (~200ms p50), and (2) a high-concurrency summarization API for notifications averaging 250 tokens per request and expected peak QPS ~1,200.

We'd like your recommendation for Dedicated capacity: which GPU SKUs to reserve (H100 / A100 / L4) and how to split reserved vs burst so we hit latency SLAs without overspending. I've attached the sample query mix (lumina_query_mix_20290509.csv).

Other constraints: SOC2 compliant VPC, predictable monthly commit, and a 6-month pilot starting June.

Can you send a recommended fleet mix and justification we can include in the exec summary?

Carlos
Head of Infrastructure
LuminaHealth

Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot sizing: memory-heavy triage flows + high QPS summary

Team — quick analysis based on the sample mix:

1) Workload breakdown (from CSV):
- 14k-window triage: ~6% of requests but accounts for ~45% of token load due to long context.
- Short summaries: ~80% of requests, average 250 tokens, high concurrency.
- Remaining are medium-context rerank/QA (~14%).

2) SKU tradeoffs (short summary):
- H100: best for low-latency long-context (14k). Higher memory headroom and attention kernel performance for 1) large KV caches and 2) minimized tiling overhead. Cost per reserved GPU significantly higher.
- A100: strong all-rounder for mid-sized contexts (2k-8k). Good throughput with mixed precision, cheaper than H100 but memory-limited for 14k windows unless we shard/tiling.
- L4: cost-efficient for short-context, high-QPS paths. Excellent tokens-per-dollar for 250-token workloads when model variants (quantized FP8/INT8) suffice. Not ideal for sustained 14k windows.

3) Ops recommendations and numbers (pilot reserve for 6 months):
- Reserved baseline: 2 x H100 (reserved) + 6 x A100 (reserved) + 8 x L4 (reserved). Rationale below.
  - H100 x2: handles simultaneous long-window sessions (we expect up to 6 concurrent heavy triage flows at peak; H100 pair with KV-cache will keep p50 under 250ms).
  - A100 x6: supports medium contexts and acts as the fallthrough for long-context requests when tiling is acceptable. Also handles batching for short jobs when L4 hits burst limits.
  - L4 x8: dedicated short-context pool for the 1,200 QPS workload (even with concurrency headroom this is cost-effective).

Estimated cost delta vs all-H100 reserve: ~35% lower monthly commit with roughly same perceived latency for the short-context tier. We'll provide a cost spreadsheet.

4) Caching/tiling/eviction:
- Use prefix/KV caching aggressively for repeated patient records; caching reduces token ops on long-context flows by ~30% in similar customers.
- For 14k windows on A100, adopt a tiling strategy: split into 8k+6k tiled segments with overlap and state stitching; expect a latency penalty ~1.6x vs H100 but still under 450ms p50 in non-congested conditions.
- Reserve eviction headroom: keep 20% spare slots in the pool to avoid OOM/eviction storms during peaks.

5) Burst plan:
- Configure Dedicated burst to Redwood hosted pool (cheaper SKUs) for non-latency-critical background workloads. For strict 200ms SLA for triage, plan for H100 fallback to be available via on-demand burst (higher cost).

6) Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: sustained long-window concurrency > planned. Mitigation: automated alerting + canary scale to add 1 H100 in 24–48 hours if required.
- Risk: model that can't quantize well. Mitigation: keep A100 headroom and an ops runbook to pin to full-precision on H100.

I'll attach a quick sensitivity spreadsheet (latency vs reserved counts).

—Ben

Agree with Ben with ops caveats and procurement-level notes:

1) H100 lead time + minimums:
- For reserved H100 pools we need a 3–4 week lead time to schedule procurement/placement (depends on region). Minimum reserve unit often in pairs — so x2 is the practical floor.
- Recommend contract language: "ability to add an H100 node within 48 hours at premium pricing" for SLA-backed triage windows.

2) Monitoring & SLA hooks:
- We must instrument token-level latency and KV cache hit rate to detect when long-context requests are being tiled/falling back. Add an alert: KV cache hit < 60% for 5 minutes -> escalate ops and consider preemptive scale.

3) Network and memory:
- For 14k windows on H100 we assume model quantized to INT8/FP8 with 90% of weights compatible; otherwise memory pressure increases and p50 suffers. Include test phase in pilot to validate quantization profile.

4) Billing and commit framing:
- Suggest a two-line commit for the pilot: (A) Reserved baseline (counts above) for predictable unit economics; (B) Burst budget cap (dollars/month) for on-demand H100 and extra A100 minutes. This avoids surprise invoice spikes.

5) Ops playbook excerpt (for proposal):
- Start pilot with reserved mix (2H100/6A100/8L4).
- Week 1: run synthetic long-context load to validate 200ms p50 on H100 with KV cache warmed (we reserve a warm-up window).
- Week 2–4: progressive ramp, monitor cache hit rate and token-per-second; if triage concurrency >6 for >30m, trigger scale to add 1 H100 and flag for contract addendum.

I'll prepare the minimum-viable SLA language and the alert thresholds to include in the proposal.

—Irene

Subject: Recommended Dedicated fleet mix and pilot guardrails — LuminaHealth

Hi Carlos,

Thanks for the details and the sample traffic. Based on our analysis (summary below) we recommend the following for the 6-month pilot so you meet the triage latency and the high-QPS cost targets:

Recommended reserved baseline (pilot):
- 2 x H100 (reserved) — dedicated long-window pool for triage flows (aim: p50 < 250ms on warmed cache).
- 6 x A100 (reserved) — mid-tier workhorse to handle medium contexts and absorb overflow from H100 with tiling if needed.
- 8 x L4 (reserved) — short-context high-QPS pool optimized with quantized model variants.

Why this split:
- H100s provide required memory headroom for 14k token windows and minimize tiling. Two nodes give redundancy and allow up to ~6 concurrent heavy sessions within latency SLA.
- A100s are cost-effective for medium contexts and are our recommended fallthrough (tiling strategy will be used there).
- L4s substantially reduce tokens-per-dollar for the 250-token paths and handle the bulk of requests.

Operational guardrails and contract notes:
- Lead time: 3–4 weeks to fully provision reserved H100s. We can schedule to meet June start if agreement is signed by May 20.
- Burst policy: include a pre-approved burst budget for on-demand H100 and extra A100 minutes. We propose a $XXk/month cap for on-demand burst during pilot; any usage beyond cap will require approval.
- Monitoring & alerts: we'll instrument KV cache hit, token-level latency, and long-window concurrency. Trigger to auto-scale/add H100: long-window concurrency >6 for >30 minutes or KV cache hit <60% sustained for 5 minutes.
- Pilot validation: week 1 synthetic validation of 14k windows (we'll warm caches) + week 2–4 progressive ramp to production traffic.

Attachments: draft proposal + sensitivity workbook attached for your review. If you want, Ben and Irene can join a call next week to walk the exec team through the tradeoffs and the SLA wording.

Next steps:
1) Confirm approval of the recommended reserved counts or tell us your budget ceiling.
2) If approved, sign the pilot commitment by 2029-05-20 to hit a June start.

Appreciate the partnership — happy to jump on a 30-min review with your infra/ procurement folks.

Best,
